item.title: Ray Marching
item.description: Explanation (skip to showcase) Ray marching is a ray based rendering technique, which can be used for 3D graphics. A ray is defined as a line which starts from a point in a specific direction, but doesn’t have a specified end point. In its most basic case called Sphere tracing, rays are sent out from the camera, each ray corresponding to a pixel. The starting point of the ray moves forwards in the direction of the ray, until the ray is close enough to the surface of an object in the scene.

item.title: L Systems
item.description: Explanation L systems carry out simple character to string replacements. You begin with a string (called the axiom) and then loop though each character in the string. Each character is then replaced by a string based on some rules. This process is repeated however many times you would like, usually called the number of iterations or the depth.
